usage: ltx-movie [-h] --story-id STORY_ID [--seed-image SEED_IMAGE]
                 [--panels PANELS] [--length LENGTH] [--fps FPS]
                 [--frames FRAMES] [--image-seed IMAGE_SEED]
                 [--video-width VIDEO_WIDTH] [--video-height VIDEO_HEIGHT]
                 [--model MODEL] [--gemma GEMMA] [--lora LORA_PATH]
                 [--stills-lora STILLS_LORA_PATH] [--character NAME]
                 [--cast PHRASE=NAME]
                 [--character-strength CHARACTER_STRENGTH]
                 [--action NAME[:STRENGTH]] [--list-characters] [--shots]
                 [--redo N[,M...]] [--story-model STORY_MODEL]
                 [--story-context-window STORY_CONTEXT_WINDOW] [--no-low-ram]
                 [--tile-frames TILE_FRAMES] [--tile-spatial TILE_SPATIAL]
                 [--panel-timeout PANEL_TIMEOUT] [--no-stills] [--no-review]
                 [--force-story] [--story-prompt-override PATH] [--force]
                 [--min-avail-gib MIN_AVAIL_GIB]
                 [--avail-timeout AVAIL_TIMEOUT]
                 [--story-server-stop-after-story | --no-story-server-stop-after-story]
                 [--story-only] [--dry-run] [--story-legacy] [--no-narration]
                 [--speech-only] [--no-auto-lora] [--judge] [--goal TEXT]
                 [narrative]

End-to-end orchestrator for the narrative-to-movie pipeline: story authoring
(bin/qwen-agent), panel 1's still (bin/ltx-story-images --only 1), manifest +
render dry-run (bin/ltx-story-manifest --chain, bin/ltx-mlx-render --dry-run),
and the chained render (bin/ltx-mlx-render), in which every clip after the
first continues from the previous clip's last frame. The wrapped phase tools
remain individually usable.

positional arguments:
  narrative             the story narrative to adapt into panels; omit only
                        when --story-prompt-override is given

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --story-id STORY_ID
  --seed-image SEED_IMAGE
                        image that becomes the movie's literal first frame:
                        Phase 0 derives the video width/height from its aspect
                        ratio (1:3 to 3:1) and attaches a scaled copy to the
                        Phase 1 story prompt; Phase 2 fits the ORIGINAL
                        (scaled, never cropped) into panel_01.png at twice the
                        video size, same as z_image, so ltx-2-mlx's own
                        downscale keeps more real detail. Incompatible with
                        --no-stills and with --video-width/--video-height.
  --panels PANELS       number of chained clips; panel 1 also gets the movie's
                        one still image; mutually exclusive with --length
  --length LENGTH       total movie length in seconds; mutually exclusive with
                        --panels. Resolved as round(length / (frames / fps))
                        -- 6.04s per panel at the defaults.
  --fps FPS
  --frames FRAMES       flat per-panel frame count; must satisfy (n-1)%8==0
                        and n>=9. 145 frames @ 24 fps = 6.04s per clip.
  --image-seed IMAGE_SEED
  --video-width VIDEO_WIDTH
  --video-height VIDEO_HEIGHT
  --model MODEL
  --gemma GEMMA         Gemma model for text encoding, passed through to
                        ltx-2-mlx's own --gemma. Override this to swap the
                        text encoder (e.g. a smaller variant on a memory-
                        constrained host); the DiT pack selected by --model is
                        unaffected.
  --lora LORA_PATH      global LoRA for the video DiT (ltx-2-mlx): repeatable;
                        PATH or PATH:STRENGTH (0 < STRENGTH <= 2, default
                        1.0). Every global LoRA applies to every panel, ahead
                        of that panel's cast-character LoRAs, at its own
                        strength (never reduced automatically). See --stills-
                        lora for the stills side.
  --stills-lora STILLS_LORA_PATH
                        global LoRA for the Phase 2 stills (z_image_skill):
                        repeatable; PATH or PATH:STRENGTH (0 < STRENGTH <= 2,
                        default 1.0). Every global LoRA applies to every
                        panel, ahead of that panel's cast-character LoRAs, at
                        its own strength (never reduced automatically). Never
                        used by --seed-image panels (there is no generation to
                        apply it to).
  --character NAME      cast a trained character from generated/characters/
                        (repeatable). For a new story, Phase 1's prompt gets a
                        Cast block with the character's fixed referring phrase
                        and description; every panel whose prompt names that
                        phrase renders with the character's LoRAs. See
                        docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-05-character-library-
                        design.md.
  --cast PHRASE=NAME    cast a trained character under PHRASE in an EXISTING
                        story.md (repeatable); PHRASE must occur in story.md
  --character-strength CHARACTER_STRENGTH
                        LoRA strength for each cast character in a panel that
                        names two or more of them (default 0.8, provisional);
                        a panel that names one cast character uses 1.0, except
                        with --shots, where every cast character uses this
                        strength
  --action NAME[:STRENGTH]
                        apply a trained action (motion) LoRA from
                        generated/actions/ to every panel (repeatable); NAME
                        or NAME:STRENGTH (0 < STRENGTH <= 2, default the
                        action's default_strength). It is fused with the
                        panel's cast-character LoRAs, so the cast performs the
                        action. Each action LoRA is checked against the video
                        base (bin/lora-check) first. See
                        docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-20-action-lora-motion-
                        library-design.md.
  --list-characters     print the character library table (the same as
                        bin/character list) and exit; must be the only
                        argument
  --shots               shots mode: every panel is its own shot with its own
                        Image: still and is rendered from that still (no
                        chaining; cuts between panels). Phase 1 uses the shots
                        story template and enforces the shot rules (one action
                        per Motion:, at most two cast characters per shot),
                        Phase 2 renders a still for every panel, and every
                        cast character LoRA defaults to 0.8. See
                        docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-shots-mode-
                        design.md.
  --redo N[,M...]       with --shots and an existing story.md: move panels
                        N,M...'s stills and clips (and movie.mp4) aside into
                        <story>/redo/<stamp>-<pid>/ and re-render only those
                        panels; every other panel is reused
  --story-model STORY_MODEL
                        model name to declare to bin/qwen-agent's --model for
                        Phase 1 story generation; must match whatever the
                        story/vision server actually reports as its model
                        (e.g. mlx_lm.server's own --model value) -- a mismatch
                        can make the server reject the request outright, not
                        just ignore the field (confirmed 2026-09-27). Omitted
                        by default: bin/qwen-agent's own default (matched to
                        the standard bin/story-server vLLM-Metal path) governs
                        unless set.
  --story-context-window STORY_CONTEXT_WINDOW
                        tokens to declare to bin/qwen-agent's --context-window
                        for Phase 1 story generation, overriding its own
                        /v1/models discovery. Needed when the story server
                        doesn't report a context-length field: bin/qwen-agent
                        then assumes a conservative 16384, which -- since
                        --max-tokens scales up with --panels and is subtracted
                        from the same window -- can make longer stories fail
                        with status=context_budget even though the real model
                        supports far more (confirmed 2026-09-27:
                        andrevp/Qwen3.5-9B-...-MLX-VLM-8bit's real window is
                        262144, 16x the wrongly-assumed default). Omitted by
                        default: bin/qwen-agent's own discovery/default
                        governs.
  --no-low-ram          ltx-2-mlx --low-ram is ON by default on this 48 GiB
                        host; this opts out. --low-ram is a weight-residency
                        change, not an algorithmic one: it costs wall-clock
                        and nothing else.
  --tile-frames TILE_FRAMES
                        escape hatch only: modality tiling denoises tiles
                        independently and blends them back, which CHANGES the
                        output and can produce seams.
  --tile-spatial TILE_SPATIAL
                        escape hatch only; see --tile-frames.
  --panel-timeout PANEL_TIMEOUT
  --no-stills           text-to-video mode: skip Phase 2 entirely (no anchor
                        stills are generated), author story.md with a
                        collapsed Prompt: field, and render every panel as
                        plain text-to-video with no conditioning image. Hard
                        cuts between panels; no continuity, no chaining.
  --no-review
  --force-story
  --story-prompt-override PATH
                        use the content of PATH verbatim as the Phase 1 story
                        prompt instead of building it from the narrative; it
                        is still persisted to story_prompt.txt. Only takes
                        effect when Phase 1 actually runs (story.md absent, or
                        --force-story).
  --force
  --min-avail-gib MIN_AVAIL_GIB
  --avail-timeout AVAIL_TIMEOUT
  --story-server-stop-after-story, --no-story-server-stop-after-story
                        after Phase 1 (story), run bin/story-server stop and
                        wait for --min-avail-gib, so Phases 2-4 get the story
                        LLM's memory back. ON by default: chained panels (2+)
                        reuse the previous clip's last frame via ffmpeg, never
                        the story server, so it is never needed past Phase 1.
                        Use --no-story-server-stop-after-story to keep it
                        resident (e.g. for rapid successive runs).
  --story-only          run Phase 0 (if --seed-image) and Phase 1 only, then
                        stop. Skips phase_release_story_server as well as
                        Phases 2-4, so a caller that regenerates story.md
                        repeatedly (e.g. bin/iterate-story) keeps the story
                        server resident across calls, with no need to also
                        pass --no-story-server-stop-after-story.
  --dry-run
  --story-legacy        Phase 1 uses the single-prompt story path (one
                        bin/qwen-agent call that writes story.md), exactly as
                        before the robust story engine. See
                        docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-17-robust-story-lora-
                        catalog-design.md.
  --no-narration        the story has no Narration: fields (no voice-over and
                        no spoken lines); panels share the length equally.
                        Needs the default story engine.
  --speech-only         Narration: is only ever a character's spoken line
                        ("the courier: ..."), never voice-over, and may be
                        empty; panels share the length equally. Needs the
                        default story engine.
  --no-auto-lora        the story plan picks no catalog LoRAs
                        (generated/loras/catalog.json); --lora/--stills-lora
                        still apply
  --judge               after the local critic rounds, run bin/judge-story
                        --patches (Claude; needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) as a final
                        gate; a minimum score below 7 applies its patches and
                        runs one more critic round
  --goal TEXT           the target output goal given to the story planner, the
                        critic and the judge, worded to complete 'The target
                        output goal is TEXT.'
